newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium gripped by rail stike over job loss fears.
newsitem.headline: Belgium gripped by rail stike over job loss fears.

text.p: Trains ground to a halt across much of Belgium on Tuesday, causing long traffic jams on the roads, as two trade unions called a 24-hour protest over feared job losses linked to a railways restructuring.

Belgium's national NMCBS/SNCB railways said there were almost no trains in the northern region of Flanders and the southern provinces of Liege, Luxembourg and Namur as well as the Brabant region around Leuven, to the east of Brussels.
Belgian radio reported a tailback of rush-hour traffic more than 30 km (20 miles) long on the E10 motorway from the northern city of Ghent into Brussels.
The Paris-Brussels-Amsterdam high speed train and Eurostar service to London were not affected. Trains were running in the Brussels region and other provinces.
Unions began their stoppage at 2000 GMT on Monday after a reconciliation meeting with management came to nothing.

The pre-announced action by the Christian and socialist unions reflects their dissatisfaction with management information policy and fears that the SNCB's Horizon 2005 restructuring and investment plan will result in job losses.
Under the plan, to be completed by 2005 and designed to make the railway profitable, the SNCB is to be split up into autonomous units.
The SNCB reacted to the strike call by noting it had hired nearly 900 workers in 1996-1997 and would hire another 4,000 before the year 2005.
The unions have also announced temporary strikes in other areas for April 22 and 25.
